newsitem.title: FRANCE: France aims for sub-two pct deficit in 2001.
newsitem.headline: France aims for sub-two pct deficit in 2001.

text.p: France, which announced an austere 1997 budget on Wednesday, plans to cut its public sector deficit to less than two percent of gross domestic product in 2001 from four percent this year, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said.

"It may not be recognised today, but economic history will say it was in 1997 that France turned its back on the ballooning of public spending and began the reduction in taxation that was so long awaited," Arthuis told a news conference to present details of the draft budget.

Arthuis said France's overall public deficit would be exactly on target at 3.0 percent of GDP next year to qualify for a single European currency, and public debt would be 58 percent of GDP, just below the 60 percent Maastricht Treaty limit.

Government spokesman Alain Lamassoure confirmed there would be cuts of 60 billion francs ($11.7 billion) in 1997 central government spending, including a reduction of around 6,000 civil service posts.
Central government spending will be frozen at this year's level, but inflation and automatic increments meant savings of 60 billion francs had to be found to achieve that goal, he said.
The main cuts will be from reducing employment and housing subsidies and stabilising France's European Union budget contribution.
